title: fix(fields): the lookup option preview never cuts a badge to a glyph (objectui#13123)
body:
Fixes #13123

Clause-②: no

Split from objectui#13115 (item 2). The trigger label and the Enter commit that objectui#13162 landed on this file are untouched.

## What was wrong

On the showcase's Account lookup (Projects, New, Account), each option's preview line read "Lifecycle: A. · Industry: Tec... · Annual Revenue: $96,00...". `previewOf` in `packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx` drew every previewed column as one `min-w-0 truncate` span, and every value inside it as another. The line shrank all columns together, in proportion to their content width. Inside each column the label (`shrink-0`) kept its width while the value took the whole cut. A badge (`max-w-full min-w-0`) fell to its 22px padding box, with its text span at zero width.

## What changes

Each previewed column is now one segment: its separator, its label and its value.

- **A badge column keeps its width.** A column whose cell is drawn by the renderer that draws a `select` badge is `shrink-0`, and its value has no clamp. The test asks the renderer map itself, so `status`, `radio`, `multiselect`, `checkboxes` and `tags` come along, and no second list of type names exists.
- **Any other column still truncates its value, never below its label.** The segment is a two-track grid: `auto` for the label, `minmax(0, max-content)` for the value. Its minimum width is therefore its label, and the value ellipsizes. The label is `whitespace-nowrap`. Without that, the `auto` track let "Annual Revenue:" wrap onto a second line; a first browser pass caught it, with the row growing from 58px to 68px.
- **A column the line cannot hold leaves whole, with every column after it.** A module-local `OptionPreviewLine` fits the line after every commit and whenever its box is resized. It shows every segment, then hides the last one shown for as long as `scrollWidth` exceeds `clientWidth`.

No export, prop, type member or language-pack key moves. The line keeps its classes and its `data-testid`, and every value keeps its `data-lookup-preview` attribute.

Why the drop is measured rather than pure CSS: a wrapping line clipped to one line's height would drop columns whole without a script, but only with a FIXED line height. A preview line can hold renderers taller than a badge (`UserCellRenderer` draws `size-8` avatars), and a fixed height would clip them. The fit reads the rendered box instead, so the line keeps its natural height.

## Browser measurement

Chromium was the preinstalled `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`, at a 1440x900 viewport. A scratch page beside the console's preview gallery (never committed) rendered the real `LookupField` against an in-memory `showcase_account` copied from the showcase object: Lifecycle and Industry as `select`, Annual Revenue as `currency` in USD. The field's box was 260, 360, 480 and 640px.

Each reading is the badge text span's `clientWidth`/`scrollWidth`; "dropped" means the segment is hidden. This container's egress refused the console's web font, so absolute pixels are fallback-font readings. Before and after use the same font.

Northwind Traders row, with the columns the showcase derives:

| field box | line | Lifecycle badge | Industry badge | Annual Revenue value | row height |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 260, before | 180 | 0/36 | 0/66 | 0/93 | 58 |
| 260, after | 180 | 36/36 | dropped | dropped | 58 |
| 360, before | 280 | 0/36 | 7/66 | 13/93 | 58 |
| 360, after | 280 | 36/36 | 66/66 | dropped | 58 |
| 480, before | 400 | 19/36 | 45/66 | 64/93 | 58 |
| 480, after | 400 | 36/36 | 66/66 | 26/93, ellipsis | 58 |
| 640, before | 560 | 36/36 | 66/66 | 93/93 | 58 |
| 640, after | 560 | 36/36 | 66/66 | 93/93 | 58 |

The full matrix covers three rows (Active, Prospect, Churned), three column layouts (the showcase's; text only; text, badge, text, badge) and four widths. Before: 29 of 36 badge renders were cut. After: 0 cut, 30 whole, 6 dropped.

Controls:
- **Text-only preview:** values still ellipsize, no label is clipped, and the row is 52px before and after at every width.
- **Row height:** unchanged in every cell of the matrix but one. In the text-first mixed layout, a 260px field drops the badge, and the row takes the 52px that a row with no badge value has today. It was 58px before, with the badge as a sliver.

## Tests

`packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.previewBadges-13123.test.tsx`, 8 tests:
- A badge column (`select` twice, `radio` once) and its value carry none of `truncate`, `min-w-0` or `overflow-hidden`. The column is `shrink-0`, and the badge sits inside the unclamped value.
- Control: a text column's value still truncates, and the column still shrinks.
- Each column is one segment holding its separator, label and value.
- With the line's widths stubbed, since jsdom has no layout: 280px shows both badges and drops revenue; 180px shows Lifecycle only; 600px shows all; 100px drops even the first badge rather than cut it. A resize brings a dropped column back and drops it again.

Ablation. The fix was committed first. `LookupField.tsx` was then replaced by its `5a8d40f` bytes under a trap that restores from `HEAD`.
- On-disk proof: the `OptionPreviewLine` count went 2, then 0, then 2; the blob read `8810a76` while mutated.
- Run: 6 failed, 2 passed. The two that pass are the text-column control and the 600px case, which hold before and after by design.
- Restore: the restored blob equals `HEAD`'s (`3d50125`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

All runs were repo-root form, through the shared verify lock, on the tree committed as `e5136a0`:
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/ packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/relationalMetaCopySet-7166.test.tsx`: 273 files passed, 1 skipped, 4199 tests passed. The second path is included because it reads this line's `data-lookup-preview`. The skipped file is the env-gated `dateCell.overdueZone-10183`, and `LookupField.pickSticks-13162` is among the passes.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check`: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields lint`: exit 0, 0 errors. Every warning is on a pre-existing line; the new test has none.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: each exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED locally: `check:eager-closure`, which needs a console production build; CI's Bundle Analysis runs it. The full lint and test farm is also CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- A hidden segment also leaves the option's accessible name, so a screen reader hears what the line shows. A truncated column used to stay in it.
- The fit runs after each commit of the row and when the line's box resizes. A badge that widens without either, such as a web-font swap after the popover opened, would stay clipped at the line's edge until the next commit; hovering a row re-renders the list. This was not observed; it is the stated bound.
- The `hidden` attribute relies on Tailwind preflight's `[hidden]` rule (`display: none` with `!important`), which the console carries.
- The issue's mechanism, read against the browser: the producer is as the card says. The cut is proportional across every column, though, not the badge losing first; the revenue value was cut too (13/93 at 360px).
